subsystems.name: Draft proposer
subsystems.role: cheaply guesses the next several tokens so the big model has something to check.
parts: small draft model (or extra prediction heads, or a lookup of common phrases)
its own sampler and KV cache

subsystems.name: Target verifier
subsystems.role: scores every drafted token in a single parallel pass instead of one at a time.

subsystems.name: Acceptance rule
subsystems.role: decides how many drafted tokens survive, in a way that leaves the output distribution unchanged.
parts: fallback resample from the corrected distribution

subsystems.name: Serving engine
subsystems.role: keeps the GPU busy and manages memory across many concurrent requests.

subsystems.name: Tuning and monitoring
subsystems.role: keeps the speed-up real rather than theoretical.

buildSteps.title: Pick the draft source
buildSteps.detail: Choose a separate small model, auxiliary prediction heads trained on the same backbone, or a non-parametric lookup of frequent continuations. The trade-off is draft quality against draft cost.

buildSteps.title: Align the vocabularies
buildSteps.detail: Draft and target must map tokens one-to-one. Any mismatch needs a projection layer or a shared tokenizer, or the comparison is meaningless.

buildSteps.title: Produce the draft
buildSteps.detail: The small model runs autoregressively for a fixed number of tokens — typically a handful — building its own KV cache as it goes.

buildSteps.title: Verify in one pass
buildSteps.detail: The drafted tokens are fed to the large model together. Because attention is causal, one forward pass yields the target's probability for every position at once; a tree-shaped mask lets several candidate branches be checked together.

buildSteps.title: Apply the acceptance test
buildSteps.detail: For each position, compare target and draft probabilities. Accept with probability equal to the ratio (capped at one), drawn from a per-token random number; on the first rejection, sample the replacement from the residual distribution and discard the rest.

buildSteps.title: Reuse the KV cache
buildSteps.detail: Accepted tokens keep their computed keys and values so they are never recomputed; rejected ones are trimmed. Cache bookkeeping is where most implementation bugs live.

buildSteps.title: Fold into the scheduler
buildSteps.detail: The engine must batch speculative requests with ordinary ones, allocate cache blocks for the extra tokens, and fall back to plain decoding when the batch is unfavourable.

buildSteps.title: Tune the draft length
buildSteps.detail: Measure acceptance rate per request type and adjust how many tokens are drafted: too few wastes the opportunity, too many wastes compute on rejected tails.

buildSteps.title: Validate exactness
buildSteps.detail: Run statistical tests comparing output distributions against plain sampling on the same prompts before trusting the speed-up in production.

prerequisites.why: verification is only cheap if many positions are scored in one fused kernel launch.
speculation multiplies cache traffic and needs paged or otherwise flexible allocation.
a draft model that disagrees with the target too often gives no speed-up at all.
the acceptance test must draw the same kind of random numbers as normal sampling to preserve the distribution.
checking several candidate branches per step needs custom masks that not every serving stack supports.

pathway.milestone: draft-model verification shipped inside major serving frameworks
pathway.unlocks: cheap low-latency chat and coding assistants without retraining the big model.

pathway.milestone: self-speculation using extra heads or retrieval lookups instead of a second model
pathway.unlocks: the same speed-up with no extra model to host or keep in sync.

pathway.milestone: models pretrained to predict several tokens per step
pathway.unlocks: higher acceptance rates because the model itself is built to be verified in blocks.

pathway.milestone: co-designed serving stacks that speculate across long context and tool calls
pathway.unlocks: real-time agents whose latency is dominated by reasoning, not by token emission.
